spans.text: | **1** | Hallucination & chunk drift | Retrieval brings in a “close enough” chunk that is actually about the wrong thing, and the model builds a confident answer on top of it.
spans.note: The prompt explicitly identifies and categorizes failure modes related to hallucination, bluffing/overconfidence, and fabrication (No.1, No.4). It encourages diagnosing these issues and provides checklists to detect when agents produce unreliable information. The guide is intentionally 'diagnostic only' and does not overstate its own scope.

spans.text: Log when each agent writes to long-term memory or updates user state. For early debugging, it is often useful to print the keys or high-level summary of what changed, without dumping full raw content.
spans.note: The prompt advises logging memory writes carefully and suggests printing only 'keys or high-level summary of what changed, without dumping full raw content.' It also highlights the importance of checking per-agent vs shared memory and user identifiers, showing awareness of data separation concerns.

spans.text: Make sure that tools which can change external state are clearly separated from read-only tools, and that each agent only receives tools that match its responsibility.
spans.note: The prompt explicitly recommends separating tools that can change external state from read-only tools, ensuring each agent only receives tools matching its responsibility, and adding limits such as maximum delegation depth and explicit stop conditions to prevent runaway behavior.

spans.text: Look for recursive or circular hand-offs, and add simple limits such as maximum delegation depth, maximum number of hops per user query and explicit “stop” conditions.
